reasoning: According to the Cambridge Bitcoin Electricity Consumption Index (CBECI) developed by the Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance (CCAF), Bitcoin's annualized electricity consumption is estimated to be between 120 TWh and 160 TWh (depending on mining difficulty and market conditions). In comparison, data from the International Energy Agency (IEA) indicates that Argentina's annual electricity consumption is approximately 130 TWh. Consequently, Bitcoin's annual electricity usage exceeds that of Argentina, as well as several other mid-sized nations.
title: Bitcoin uses more electricity than Argentina
